propositions: A commit landing between verify and sign steps causes verify to check one HEAD revision and sign to see a different unrelated HEAD revision, splitting the atomicity of the close operation.
When drift is detected between verify and sign, the close transition proceeds anyway, closing the ticket without a completion attestation while refusing to sign the stale tree.
The suggested recovery ('re-close to certify') is a no-op because the ticket is already closed, leaving no non-force path to obtain the completion attestation.
The default code path (no --ref argument) reads HEAD twice independently instead of pinning a single revision for the entire verify+sign+close unit.
An already-closed ticket lacking a completion signature has no first-class recovery mechanism short of --force-close or manual manifest fabrication.
